questions.question: In “A Fable for Tomorrow,” how does Rachel Carson use the “checkerboard” image to connect human settlement with agriculture and order?
questions.solution_html:
• In “A Fable for Tomorrow,” how does Rachel Carson use the “checkerboard” image to connect
  • human settlement with agriculture and order? / [CO1]
  • Answer: Carson uses the image of a “checkerboard” to describe the neatly arranged fields and
  • farms of rural America. -- image suggests human effort to organise nature into systematic,
  • controlled patterns -- land is divided into geometric sections, reflecting agricultural planning and
  • human intervention -- conveys a sense of harmony between human settlement and the natural
  • environment -- hints at human dominance over nature. -- once orderly “checkerboard” turns
  • silent and lifeless, emphasise fragility of human-imposed order
questions.source_exam: MGU-UGP (HONOURS) 2024 Admission Regular Exam Sem 4, March 2026

questions.question: Examine how "Plastik" employs a child’s imagination to communicate its environmental message.
questions.solution_html:
• Examine how "Plastik" employs a child’s imagination to communicate its environmental
  • message. / [CO3]
  • Answer: Plastik uses a child’s perspective to simplify a complex issue --playful imagination --
  • plastic waste is transformed into vivid, fantastical images. This creative lens makes pollution
  • appear both familiar and disturbing. The innocence of the child contrasts sharply with the
  • severity of environmental damage -- suggests what seems harmless in daily life accumulates
  • into long-term ecological harm
